contract.reader: A student or engineer who knows matrix multiplication and trigonometry, has read the series first entry and is about to meet arm kinematics and state estimation
contract.problem: Every sensor and link reports positions in its own frame; the reader needs a precise, mechanical way to convert positions and orientations between frames and to avoid the usual frame bugs
contract.outcome: Build and invert 2D and 3D rotation matrices and homogeneous transforms; explain why 3D rotations do not commute; choose among rotation matrices, Euler angles, axis-angle and quaternions knowing gimbal lock and the q/-q ambiguity; chain transforms through a frame tree; recognize the common frame mistakes
contract.contribution: Label-cancelling notation used consistently from definition to a worked mobile-robot example and a frame tree, with a table of common mistakes and their symptoms
contract.evidence: Derivations and worked numbers; three exercises with answers; Craig (2005), Lynch and Park (2017), Siciliano et al. (2009)
contract.limitations: No derivation of quaternion multiplication or slerp; Euler conventions beyond yaw-pitch-roll only counted; no code

findings.problem: Side-by-side display equations are wider than the column; the second product of Section 3.2 is cut at 1280 px and hidden at 360 px; at 360 px also the second equation of 2.1, the matrix K of Rodrigues' formula, the inverse translation of 4.3 and the results of the Section 5 worked example are hidden
findings.whyItMatters: Section 3.2 exists to show the two products differ, and the worked example's answers are the page's main demonstration; the hidden parts scroll sideways with no cue
findings.action: Put each pair on separate lines (one equation per display or an aligned/gathered block); set Rx, Ry, Rz one per line
findings.acceptance: On new captures both products of 3.2 and Rz are fully visible at 1280 px, and every listed equation is fully visible at 360 px, light and dark

findings.problem: Possessives after inline math render with a left single quotation mark (B‘s, A‘s) instead of an apostrophe
findings.whyItMatters: Visible typographic error three times in core sections
findings.action: Write ’ after the math in the source or rephrase (the axes of B)
findings.acceptance: The three possessives show an apostrophe on the live page
